## CHANGES

This policy contract, your insurance application (which is made a part of this policy as if attached hereto), the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy issued by us , contain all the agreements between you and us .   Subject to the following, the terms of this policy may not be changed or waived except by an endorsement issued by us .

The premium for this policy is based on information we received from you and other sources. You agree to cooperate with us in determining if this information is correct and complete, and to promptly notify us if it changes during the policy period. If this information is determined by us to be incorrect, incomplete, or if it changes during the policy period, you agree that we may adjust your policy information and premium accordingly. Changes that may result in a premium adjustment are contained in our rates and rules. These include, but are not limited to, you , a relative , or a rated resident obtaining a driver's license or operator's permit, or changes in:

- 1 . the number, type or use classification of covered autos ;
2. the persons who regularly operate a covered auto ;
3. the persons of legal driving age residing in your household;
4. the residents in your household;
5. an operator's marital status;
6. your mailing address and your residence address;
- 7 . the principal garaging address of any covered auto ;
8. coverage, deductibles, or limits of liability; or
9. rating territory or discount eligibility .

The coverage provided in your policy may be changed only by the issuance of a new policy or an endorsement by us .  However, if during the policy period we broaden any coverage afforded under the current edition of your policy without additional premium charge, that change will automatically apply to your policy as of the date the coverage change is implemented in your state.

If you ask us to delete a vehicle from this policy , no coverage will apply to that vehicle as of the date and time you ask us to delete it.

## DUTY TO REPORT CHANGES

You must promptly report to us all changes, including additions and deletions, in policy information. This includes, but is not limited to, changes in:

- 1 . your mailing address or your residence address;
2. the principal garaging address of any covered auto ;
3. the residents in your household;
4. the persons of legal driving age residing in your household;
5. the persons who regularly operate a covered auto ;
6. an operator's marital status; or
- 7 . the driver's license or operator's permit status of you , a relative , or a rated resident.

## SETTLEMENT OF CLAIMS

We may use estimating, appraisal, or injury evaluation systems to assist us in adjusting claims under this policy and to assist us in determining the amount of damages, expenses, or loss payable under this policy . Such systems may be developed by us or a third party and may include computer software, databases, and specialized technology.

## TERMS OF POLICY CONFORMED TO STATUTES

If any provision of this policy fails to conform to the statutes of the state listed on your application as your residence, the provision shall be deemed amended to conform to such statutes. All other provisions shall be given full force and effect. Any disputes as to the coverages provided or the provisions of this policy shall be governed by the law of the state listed on your application as your residence.

## TRANSFER OF INTEREST

The rights and duties under this policy may not be transferred to another person without our written consent. However, if a named insured shown on the declarations page dies, this policy will provide coverage until the end of the policy period for the legal representative of the named insured, while acting as such, and for persons covered under this policy on the date of the named insured's death.

## FRAUD OR MISREPRESENTATION

Any changes we make at your request to this policy after inception will be made in reliance upon information you provide. If you :

- 1 . make incorrect statements or representations to us with regard to any material fact or circumstance;
2. conceal or misrepresent any material fact or circumstance; or
3. engage in fraudulent conduct;

we may deny coverage for an accident or loss if you , in connection with any requested change, or at any time during the policy period, have concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance or engaged in fraudulent conduct and that concealment, misrepresentation, or fraudulent conduct was material to a risk we assumed.

We may deny coverage for an accident or loss if you or a person seeking coverage has concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, or engaged in fraudulent conduct which materially affects our interests, in connection with the presentation or settlement of a claim.

## CANCELLATION

You may cancel this policy during the policy period by calling or writing us and stating the future date you wish the cancellation to be effective.

We may cancel this policy during the policy period by mailing a notice of cancellation to the named insured shown on the declarations page at the last known address appearing in our records.

If the policy is cancelled for nonpayment of premium, we will mail notice of cancellation to you at least 15 days before cancellation takes effect. In all other cases, we will mail notice of cancellation to you at least 25 days before the cancellation takes effect.

We may cancel this policy for any reason if the notice is received by the named insured within the first 59 days of the initial policy period.

After this policy is in effect for more than 59 days, or if this is a renewal or continuation policy , we may cancel only for one or more of the following reasons:

- 1 . nonpayment of premium;
2. material misrepresentation or fraud by you with respect to any material fact in the procurement, continuation, change or renewal of this policy;
3. material misrepresentation or fraud in the submission of any claim under this policy;
4. loss of driving privileges through suspension, revocation or expiration of an operator's license issued to you , any driver in your household, or any regular operator of a covered auto , other than the first or second suspension under:
- a. Title 29-A M.R.S.A §2471(2);
- b. Title 29-A M.R.S.A §2472(2); or
- c. Title 28-A M.R.S.A §2052;
5. loss of driving privileges by you , a relative , a rated resident , or a principal operator of a covered auto through revocation of an operator's license during the policy period or if this policy is a renewal, during its policy period or the 180 days immediately preceding its effective date; or
6. violation of the terms or conditions of this policy .

If this policy is cancelled, coverage will not be provided as of the effective date and time shown in the notice of cancellation. ## CANCELLATION REFUND

Upon cancellation, you may be entitled to a premium refund. However, our making or offering of a refund is not a condition of cancellation.

If this policy is cancelled, any refund due will be computed on a daily pro rata basis. However, we will retain a cancellation fee if this policy is cancelled at your request or if cancellation is for nonpayment of premium. A cancellation fee will be charged only during the initial policy period.

## NONRENEWAL

A postal service certificate of mailing to the named insured at the insured's last known address appearing in our records will be sufficient proof of notice. Notice will be mailed more than 33 days before the end of the policy period.

## AUTOMATIC TERMINATION

If we or an affiliate offers to renew or continue this policy and you or your representative does not accept, this policy will automatically terminate at the end of the current policy period. Failure to pay the required renewal or continuation premium when due will mean that you have not accepted our offer.

If you obtain other insurance on a covered auto , any similar insurance provided by this policy will terminate as to that covered auto on the effective date of the other insurance.

If a covered auto is sold or transferred to someone other than you or a relative , any insurance provided by this policy will terminate as to that covered auto on the effective date of the sale or transfer.

2|Insured Persons, Household Members, and Insurance Coverage Dynamics|"# Insured Persons, Household Members, and Insurance Coverage Dynamics

The community centers on the interconnected roles of insured persons, household members (including relatives and rated residents), and key insurance policy components such as liability, medical payments, and claims processes. These entities are linked through relationships involving coverage eligibility, premium adjustments, legal recovery mechanisms, and dispute resolution. The structure reflects a complex network where household composition, driving status, and legal actions directly influence insurance outcomes, with significant implications for risk assessment, financial liability, and claim resolution.

## Insured Persons as Central Nodes in Coverage and Liability

The term 'INSURED PERSON' serves as a foundational concept in the community, encompassing the policyholder, relatives, rated residents, and any individual operating a covered auto with permission. This broad definition ensures that multiple individuals within a household are protected under the policy, particularly for liability and medical payments coverage. The inclusion of insured persons extends to those involved in ride-sharing activities, provided the activity falls within the policy’s defined scope, indicating a flexible yet structured approach to coverage. Their status as insured persons enables them to file claims for bodily injury, medical expenses, and even loss of earnings, subject to policy limits and insurer approval. This expansive definition underscores the policy’s intent to protect not only the primary policyholder but also a wide range of household members and temporary operators, reinforcing the household-centric nature of the insurance framework [Data: Entities (24), Relationships (49, 124, 82, 186, 386, +more)].

## Household Composition Drives Coverage and Premium Determination

The presence and status of household members—specifically relatives and rated residents—play a critical role in shaping both coverage eligibility and premium costs. Relatives, defined as family members connected by blood, marriage, adoption, or legal guardianship, are considered part of the household and may be covered under the policy when using a covered vehicle with permission. This inclusion extends to dependents temporarily away from home, emphasizing the policy’s focus on household unity. Rated residents, though not related by blood or marriage, are formally listed on the policy and are treated as household members for rating purposes. Their driving record and status directly influence premium calculations, and their inclusion can trigger premium adjustments, especially if they obtain a driver’s license. The relationship between rated residents and the household is formalized through the 'RATED RESIDENT' entity, which is explicitly tied to the household via the 'HOUSEHOLD' entity, reinforcing the importance of accurate household composition in underwriting [Data: Entities (151, 23, 22, 255), Relationships (47, 48, 357, 336, 239, +more)].

## Legal and Financial Mechanisms for Claim Recovery and Reimbursement

The community includes a robust set of legal and financial mechanisms that govern how insured persons recover damages and reimburse insurers. A key requirement for suing the insurer is a judgment after trial against the insured person, which establishes legal liability and enables the insurer to be held accountable for payments under Part I—Liability to Others. Similarly, collection activity by a medical service provider must occur before an insured person can pursue legal action against the insurer for denied medical expenses. These procedural prerequisites ensure that claims are validated through formal legal channels. Additionally, when recovery is obtained from a liable party, the insured person is responsible for holding the funds in trust and reimbursing the insurer up to the insurer’s pro rata share, which is calculated based on the amount paid out under the policy. This mechanism ensures that insurers are not overburdened and that recovery is distributed fairly between the insured and the insurer [Data: Entities (273, 100, 277, 276), Relationships (386, 390, 391, 125, +more)].

## Dispute Resolution Through Arbitration and Written Agreements

Disputes over claims are resolved through formal processes such as arbitration proceedings and written agreements. Arbitration proceedings are binding and governed by local rules, allowing arbitrators to determine liability and damages in cases where a dispute arises. The insurer may participate in these proceedings, particularly when liability is contested or when the operator or owner of an uninsured vehicle is involved. A written agreement between the insured, claimant, and insurer can serve as a basis for legal action against the insurer, provided all parties are involved. This agreement is a prerequisite for the insurer to be sued, ensuring that claims are settled through structured negotiation before litigation. These mechanisms reflect a tiered approach to dispute resolution, balancing efficiency with legal enforceability, and are critical in maintaining the integrity of the claims process [Data: Entities (151, 274, 276), Relationships (218, 192, 387, 388, +more)].

## Premium Adjustments Triggered by Household and Behavioral Changes

Premium adjustments are a dynamic feature of the insurance framework, triggered by changes in household composition, driving status, or geographic location. A rated resident obtaining a driver’s license is a direct trigger for a premium adjustment, reflecting the increased risk associated with adding a new driver to the household. Similarly, changes in the rating territory—such as moving to a higher-risk area—can result in a premium adjustment, as the insurer recalculates risk based on new geographic data. These adjustments ensure that premiums remain aligned with current risk profiles. The relationship between premium adjustments and rated residents is particularly strong, with multiple records indicating that the addition or change in status of a rated resident directly impacts the policy’s cost. This responsiveness to household dynamics highlights the insurer’s focus on real-time risk assessment and financial fairness [Data: Entities (235, 244, 247), Relationships (336, 340, 359, +more)].

## Coverage for Ancillary Risks: Pet Injury and Child Safety Seat Damage

Beyond traditional auto liability and medical coverage, the policy extends protection to ancillary risks such as pet injury and child safety seat damage. Your pet, defined as a dog or cat owned by the policyholder, a relative, or a rated resident, may be eligible for coverage under Pet Injury Coverage if injured or killed during a covered auto loss. This provision reflects the policy’s inclusive approach to household assets. Similarly, damage to a child safety seat during an accident is covered under collision coverage, with reimbursement provided to the insured person. These extensions demonstrate that the insurance framework is not limited to vehicle and driver risks but also accounts for the well-being of household members and their belongings. The inclusion of these coverages reinforces the policy’s holistic view of household risk and its commitment to comprehensive protection [Data: Entities (156, 146), Relationships (239, 186, +more)].

## Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage as a Critical Safety Net

Part III Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage is a vital component of the insurance community, providing protection when the at-fault driver lacks sufficient insurance or is uninsured. This coverage ensures that insured persons are not left financially vulnerable in accidents involving drivers who cannot pay for damages. It applies when the at-fault driver is either uninsured or underinsured, and the insured person can file a claim to recover damages. This coverage is particularly important in high-risk environments where uninsured drivers are common. The relationship between this coverage and the insured person is direct and essential, as it serves as a financial safety net that complements other liability and medical payments protections. Its presence underscores the policy’s focus on risk mitigation and financial security for policyholders [Data: Entities (50), Relationships (82, +more)].

## The Role of the Principal Garaging Address in Coverage and Risk Assessment

The principal garaging address—the primary location where a covered auto is parked and stored—plays a significant role in determining both coverage and premium. This address is a key factor in risk assessment, as insurers use it to evaluate local accident rates, theft risks, and other location-specific variables. The garaging address is tied to the policy through the 'PRINCIPAL GARAGING ADDRESS' entity, which influences the policy’s terms and conditions. Accidents and losses occurring while a covered auto is being transported between ports may also be covered, indicating that the garaging address is not the only factor but is central to the insurer’s risk model. This geographic anchor ensures that coverage is tailored to the actual risk profile of the vehicle’s primary location, enhancing the accuracy of underwriting and claims management [Data: Entities (248), Relationships (361, +more)]."

2|Insured Persons, Household Members, and Insurance Coverage Dynamics|"# Insured Persons, Household Members, and Insurance Coverage Dynamics

The community centers on the interconnected roles of insured persons, household members (including relatives and rated residents), and key insurance policy components such as liability, medical payments, and claims processes. These entities are linked through relationships involving coverage eligibility, premium adjustments, legal recovery mechanisms, and dispute resolution. The structure reflects a complex network where household composition, driving status, and legal actions directly influence insurance outcomes, with significant implications for risk assessment, financial liability, and claim resolution.

## Insured Persons as Central Nodes in Coverage and Liability

The term 'INSURED PERSON' serves as a foundational concept in the community, encompassing the policyholder, relatives, rated residents, and any individual operating a covered auto with permission. This broad definition ensures that multiple individuals within a household are protected under the policy, particularly for liability and medical payments coverage. The inclusion of insured persons extends to those involved in ride-sharing activities, provided the activity falls within the policy’s defined scope, indicating a flexible yet structured approach to coverage. Their status as insured persons enables them to file claims for bodily injury, medical expenses, and even loss of earnings, subject to policy limits and insurer approval. This expansive definition underscores the policy’s intent to protect not only the primary policyholder but also a wide range of household members and temporary operators, reinforcing the household-centric nature of the insurance framework [Data: Entities (24), Relationships (49, 124, 82, 186, 386, +more)].

## Household Composition Drives Coverage and Premium Determination

The presence and status of household members—specifically relatives and rated residents—play a critical role in shaping both coverage eligibility and premium costs. Relatives, defined as family members connected by blood, marriage, adoption, or legal guardianship, are considered part of the household and may be covered under the policy when using a covered vehicle with permission. This inclusion extends to dependents temporarily away from home, emphasizing the policy’s focus on household unity. Rated residents, though not related by blood or marriage, are formally listed on the policy and are treated as household members for rating purposes. Their driving record and status directly influence premium calculations, and their inclusion can trigger premium adjustments, especially if they obtain a driver’s license. The relationship between rated residents and the household is formalized through the 'RATED RESIDENT' entity, which is explicitly tied to the household via the 'HOUSEHOLD' entity, reinforcing the importance of accurate household composition in underwriting [Data: Entities (151, 23, 22, 255), Relationships (47, 48, 357, 336, 239, +more)].

## Legal and Financial Mechanisms for Claim Recovery and Reimbursement

The community includes a robust set of legal and financial mechanisms that govern how insured persons recover damages and reimburse insurers. A key requirement for suing the insurer is a judgment after trial against the insured person, which establishes legal liability and enables the insurer to be held accountable for payments under Part I—Liability to Others. Similarly, collection activity by a medical service provider must occur before an insured person can pursue legal action against the insurer for denied medical expenses. These procedural prerequisites ensure that claims are validated through formal legal channels. Additionally, when recovery is obtained from a liable party, the insured person is responsible for holding the funds in trust and reimbursing the insurer up to the insurer’s pro rata share, which is calculated based on the amount paid out under the policy. This mechanism ensures that insurers are not overburdened and that recovery is distributed fairly between the insured and the insurer [Data: Entities (273, 100, 277, 276), Relationships (386, 390, 391, 125, +more)].

## Dispute Resolution Through Arbitration and Written Agreements

Disputes over claims are resolved through formal processes such as arbitration proceedings and written agreements. Arbitration proceedings are binding and governed by local rules, allowing arbitrators to determine liability and damages in cases where a dispute arises. The insurer may participate in these proceedings, particularly when liability is contested or when the operator or owner of an uninsured vehicle is involved. A written agreement between the insured, claimant, and insurer can serve as a basis for legal action against the insurer, provided all parties are involved. This agreement is a prerequisite for the insurer to be sued, ensuring that claims are settled through structured negotiation before litigation. These mechanisms reflect a tiered approach to dispute resolution, balancing efficiency with legal enforceability, and are critical in maintaining the integrity of the claims process [Data: Entities (151, 274, 276), Relationships (218, 192, 387, 388, +more)].

## Premium Adjustments Triggered by Household and Behavioral Changes

Premium adjustments are a dynamic feature of the insurance framework, triggered by changes in household composition, driving status, or geographic location. A rated resident obtaining a driver’s license is a direct trigger for a premium adjustment, reflecting the increased risk associated with adding a new driver to the household. Similarly, changes in the rating territory—such as moving to a higher-risk area—can result in a premium adjustment, as the insurer recalculates risk based on new geographic data. These adjustments ensure that premiums remain aligned with current risk profiles. The relationship between premium adjustments and rated residents is particularly strong, with multiple records indicating that the addition or change in status of a rated resident directly impacts the policy’s cost. This responsiveness to household dynamics highlights the insurer’s focus on real-time risk assessment and financial fairness [Data: Entities (235, 244, 247), Relationships (336, 340, 359, +more)].

## Coverage for Ancillary Risks: Pet Injury and Child Safety Seat Damage

Beyond traditional auto liability and medical coverage, the policy extends protection to ancillary risks such as pet injury and child safety seat damage. Your pet, defined as a dog or cat owned by the policyholder, a relative, or a rated resident, may be eligible for coverage under Pet Injury Coverage if injured or killed during a covered auto loss. This provision reflects the policy’s inclusive approach to household assets. Similarly, damage to a child safety seat during an accident is covered under collision coverage, with reimbursement provided to the insured person. These extensions demonstrate that the insurance framework is not limited to vehicle and driver risks but also accounts for the well-being of household members and their belongings. The inclusion of these coverages reinforces the policy’s holistic view of household risk and its commitment to comprehensive protection [Data: Entities (156, 146), Relationships (239, 186, +more)].

## Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage as a Critical Safety Net

Part III Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage is a vital component of the insurance community, providing protection when the at-fault driver lacks sufficient insurance or is uninsured. This coverage ensures that insured persons are not left financially vulnerable in accidents involving drivers who cannot pay for damages. It applies when the at-fault driver is either uninsured or underinsured, and the insured person can file a claim to recover damages. This coverage is particularly important in high-risk environments where uninsured drivers are common. The relationship between this coverage and the insured person is direct and essential, as it serves as a financial safety net that complements other liability and medical payments protections. Its presence underscores the policy’s focus on risk mitigation and financial security for policyholders [Data: Entities (50), Relationships (82, +more)].

## The Role of the Principal Garaging Address in Coverage and Risk Assessment

The principal garaging address—the primary location where a covered auto is parked and stored—plays a significant role in determining both coverage and premium. This address is a key factor in risk assessment, as insurers use it to evaluate local accident rates, theft risks, and other location-specific variables. The garaging address is tied to the policy through the 'PRINCIPAL GARAGING ADDRESS' entity, which influences the policy’s terms and conditions. Accidents and losses occurring while a covered auto is being transported between ports may also be covered, indicating that the garaging address is not the only factor but is central to the insurer’s risk model. This geographic anchor ensures that coverage is tailored to the actual risk profile of the vehicle’s primary location, enhancing the accuracy of underwriting and claims management [Data: Entities (248), Relationships (361, +more)]."

2|Insured Persons, Household Members, and Insurance Coverage Dynamics|"# Insured Persons, Household Members, and Insurance Coverage Dynamics

The community centers on the interconnected roles of insured persons, household members (including relatives and rated residents), and key insurance policy components such as liability, medical payments, and claims processes. These entities are linked through relationships involving coverage eligibility, premium adjustments, legal recovery mechanisms, and dispute resolution. The structure reflects a complex network where household composition, driving status, and legal actions directly influence insurance outcomes, with significant implications for risk assessment, financial liability, and claim resolution.

## Insured Persons as Central Nodes in Coverage and Liability

The term 'INSURED PERSON' serves as a foundational concept in the community, encompassing the policyholder, relatives, rated residents, and any individual operating a covered auto with permission. This broad definition ensures that multiple individuals within a household are protected under the policy, particularly for liability and medical payments coverage. The inclusion of insured persons extends to those involved in ride-sharing activities, provided the activity falls within the policy’s defined scope, indicating a flexible yet structured approach to coverage. Their status as insured persons enables them to file claims for bodily injury, medical expenses, and even loss of earnings, subject to policy limits and insurer approval. This expansive definition underscores the policy’s intent to protect not only the primary policyholder but also a wide range of household members and temporary operators, reinforcing the household-centric nature of the insurance framework [Data: Entities (24), Relationships (49, 124, 82, 186, 386, +more)].

## Household Composition Drives Coverage and Premium Determination

The presence and status of household members—specifically relatives and rated residents—play a critical role in shaping both coverage eligibility and premium costs. Relatives, defined as family members connected by blood, marriage, adoption, or legal guardianship, are considered part of the household and may be covered under the policy when using a covered vehicle with permission. This inclusion extends to dependents temporarily away from home, emphasizing the policy’s focus on household unity. Rated residents, though not related by blood or marriage, are formally listed on the policy and are treated as household members for rating purposes. Their driving record and status directly influence premium calculations, and their inclusion can trigger premium adjustments, especially if they obtain a driver’s license. The relationship between rated residents and the household is formalized through the 'RATED RESIDENT' entity, which is explicitly tied to the household via the 'HOUSEHOLD' entity, reinforcing the importance of accurate household composition in underwriting [Data: Entities (151, 23, 22, 255), Relationships (47, 48, 357, 336, 239, +more)].

## Legal and Financial Mechanisms for Claim Recovery and Reimbursement

The community includes a robust set of legal and financial mechanisms that govern how insured persons recover damages and reimburse insurers. A key requirement for suing the insurer is a judgment after trial against the insured person, which establishes legal liability and enables the insurer to be held accountable for payments under Part I—Liability to Others. Similarly, collection activity by a medical service provider must occur before an insured person can pursue legal action against the insurer for denied medical expenses. These procedural prerequisites ensure that claims are validated through formal legal channels. Additionally, when recovery is obtained from a liable party, the insured person is responsible for holding the funds in trust and reimbursing the insurer up to the insurer’s pro rata share, which is calculated based on the amount paid out under the policy. This mechanism ensures that insurers are not overburdened and that recovery is distributed fairly between the insured and the insurer [Data: Entities (273, 100, 277, 276), Relationships (386, 390, 391, 125, +more)].

## Dispute Resolution Through Arbitration and Written Agreements

Disputes over claims are resolved through formal processes such as arbitration proceedings and written agreements. Arbitration proceedings are binding and governed by local rules, allowing arbitrators to determine liability and damages in cases where a dispute arises. The insurer may participate in these proceedings, particularly when liability is contested or when the operator or owner of an uninsured vehicle is involved. A written agreement between the insured, claimant, and insurer can serve as a basis for legal action against the insurer, provided all parties are involved. This agreement is a prerequisite for the insurer to be sued, ensuring that claims are settled through structured negotiation before litigation. These mechanisms reflect a tiered approach to dispute resolution, balancing efficiency with legal enforceability, and are critical in maintaining the integrity of the claims process [Data: Entities (151, 274, 276), Relationships (218, 192, 387, 388, +more)].

## Premium Adjustments Triggered by Household and Behavioral Changes

Premium adjustments are a dynamic feature of the insurance framework, triggered by changes in household composition, driving status, or geographic location. A rated resident obtaining a driver’s license is a direct trigger for a premium adjustment, reflecting the increased risk associated with adding a new driver to the household. Similarly, changes in the rating territory—such as moving to a higher-risk area—can result in a premium adjustment, as the insurer recalculates risk based on new geographic data. These adjustments ensure that premiums remain aligned with current risk profiles. The relationship between premium adjustments and rated residents is particularly strong, with multiple records indicating that the addition or change in status of a rated resident directly impacts the policy’s cost. This responsiveness to household dynamics highlights the insurer’s focus on real-time risk assessment and financial fairness [Data: Entities (235, 244, 247), Relationships (336, 340, 359, +more)].

## Coverage for Ancillary Risks: Pet Injury and Child Safety Seat Damage

Beyond traditional auto liability and medical coverage, the policy extends protection to ancillary risks such as pet injury and child safety seat damage. Your pet, defined as a dog or cat owned by the policyholder, a relative, or a rated resident, may be eligible for coverage under Pet Injury Coverage if injured or killed during a covered auto loss. This provision reflects the policy’s inclusive approach to household assets. Similarly, damage to a child safety seat during an accident is covered under collision coverage, with reimbursement provided to the insured person. These extensions demonstrate that the insurance framework is not limited to vehicle and driver risks but also accounts for the well-being of household members and their belongings. The inclusion of these coverages reinforces the policy’s holistic view of household risk and its commitment to comprehensive protection [Data: Entities (156, 146), Relationships (239, 186, +more)].

## Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage as a Critical Safety Net

Part III Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage is a vital component of the insurance community, providing protection when the at-fault driver lacks sufficient insurance or is uninsured. This coverage ensures that insured persons are not left financially vulnerable in accidents involving drivers who cannot pay for damages. It applies when the at-fault driver is either uninsured or underinsured, and the insured person can file a claim to recover damages. This coverage is particularly important in high-risk environments where uninsured drivers are common. The relationship between this coverage and the insured person is direct and essential, as it serves as a financial safety net that complements other liability and medical payments protections. Its presence underscores the policy’s focus on risk mitigation and financial security for policyholders [Data: Entities (50), Relationships (82, +more)].

## The Role of the Principal Garaging Address in Coverage and Risk Assessment

The principal garaging address—the primary location where a covered auto is parked and stored—plays a significant role in determining both coverage and premium. This address is a key factor in risk assessment, as insurers use it to evaluate local accident rates, theft risks, and other location-specific variables. The garaging address is tied to the policy through the 'PRINCIPAL GARAGING ADDRESS' entity, which influences the policy’s terms and conditions. Accidents and losses occurring while a covered auto is being transported between ports may also be covered, indicating that the garaging address is not the only factor but is central to the insurer’s risk model. This geographic anchor ensures that coverage is tailored to the actual risk profile of the vehicle’s primary location, enhancing the accuracy of underwriting and claims management [Data: Entities (248), Relationships (361, +more)]."

- 1 . the amount shown for 'each person' is the most we will pay for all damages due to bodily injury to one person resulting from any one accident;

3|Claims Settlement Systems and the Insurer|"# Claims Settlement Systems and the Insurer

The community centers on the claims settlement process within the insurance industry, with the insurer as the primary actor utilizing three specialized systems—estimating, appraisal, and injury evaluation—to assess and process claims. These systems are integral components of the settlement process, each contributing to the evaluation of damages, property value, and injury-related costs. The relationships between the settlement process and these systems are direct and functionally critical, indicating a tightly integrated operational framework.

## Claims Settlement as the central process

The claims settlement process is the foundational entity in this community, serving as the overarching mechanism through which insurers evaluate and resolve claims. It involves the use of specialized tools and methodologies to determine appropriate payouts, ensuring consistency and accuracy in claim adjudication. This process is essential to the functioning of the insurance system, as it directly impacts customer satisfaction, financial liability, and regulatory compliance. [Data: Entities (239), Relationships (342, 343, 344, 345)]

## Estimating System supports claim evaluation

The estimating system is a key technical tool used by insurers to assess the financial value of damages or losses in claims. It may be developed internally or sourced from third-party providers, and it plays a critical role in determining initial payout estimates. By providing data-driven assessments, the estimating system helps streamline the claims process and reduce processing time. Its integration into the settlement process ensures that claims are evaluated with a degree of objectivity and standardization. [Data: Entities (249), Relationships (343)]

## Appraisal System ensures formal valuation

The appraisal system is a formalized method used to evaluate the value of property or injuries in claims, often involving certified professionals or standardized protocols. This system is particularly important in high-value or complex claims where accuracy is paramount. By providing a structured and verifiable assessment, the appraisal system enhances the credibility of the settlement outcome and reduces the risk of disputes. Its use within the settlement process underscores the importance of objective valuation in insurance operations. [Data: Entities (250), Relationships (344)]

## Injury Evaluation System integrates medical and financial data

The injury evaluation system is specifically designed to assess the extent of physical injuries and their associated financial implications in claims. It may involve input from medical professionals, diagnostic data, and established medical-legal guidelines. This system ensures that compensation for personal injury claims reflects both the severity of the injury and the projected long-term costs, such as medical treatment and lost wages. Its integration into the settlement process highlights the interdisciplinary nature of modern claims handling. [Data: Entities (251), Relationships (345)]

## Insurer as the central actor in the settlement ecosystem

The insurer is the primary entity responsible for managing the claims settlement process and deploying the supporting systems. It uses the estimating, appraisal, and injury evaluation systems to adjust claims and determine payouts, indicating a high degree of operational dependency on these tools. The insurer’s role is not merely administrative but strategic, as the accuracy and efficiency of these systems directly affect financial risk, customer trust, and regulatory standing. The strong relationship between the insurer and the settlement process underscores its central position in the community. [Data: Relationships (342)]

## Interdependence of systems within the settlement process

The three systems—estimating, appraisal, and injury evaluation—are not isolated tools but are functionally interdependent within the claims settlement process. Each system contributes a distinct layer of assessment: estimating for initial damage valuation, appraisal for formal property or injury assessment, and injury evaluation for medical cost projection. Their combined use ensures a comprehensive and multi-faceted evaluation of claims, reducing the likelihood of under- or overpayment. This interdependence reflects a mature, integrated claims management framework. [Data: Relationships (343, 344, 345)]"

## CHANGES

This policy contract, your insurance application (which is made a part of this policy as if attached hereto), the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy issued by us , contain all the agreements between you and us .   Subject to the following, the terms of this policy may not be changed or waived except by an endorsement issued by us .

The premium for this policy is based on information we received from you and other sources. You agree to cooperate with us in determining if this information is correct and complete, and to promptly notify us if it changes during the policy period. If this information is determined by us to be incorrect, incomplete, or if it changes during the policy period, you agree that we may adjust your policy information and premium accordingly. Changes that may result in a premium adjustment are contained in our rates and rules. These include, but are not limited to, you , a relative , or a rated resident obtaining a driver's license or operator's permit, or changes in:

- 1 . the number, type or use classification of covered autos ;
2. the persons who regularly operate a covered auto ;
3. the persons of legal driving age residing in your household;
4. the residents in your household;
5. an operator's marital status;
6. your mailing address and your residence address;
- 7 . the principal garaging address of any covered auto ;
8. coverage, deductibles, or limits of liability; or
9. rating territory or discount eligibility .

The coverage provided in your policy may be changed only by the issuance of a new policy or an endorsement by us .  However, if during the policy period we broaden any coverage afforded under the current edition of your policy without additional premium charge, that change will automatically apply to your policy as of the date the coverage change is implemented in your state.

If you ask us to delete a vehicle from this policy , no coverage will apply to that vehicle as of the date and time you ask us to delete it.

## DUTY TO REPORT CHANGES

You must promptly report to us all changes, including additions and deletions, in policy information. This includes, but is not limited to, changes in:

- 1 . your mailing address or your residence address;
2. the principal garaging address of any covered auto ;
3. the residents in your household;
4. the persons of legal driving age residing in your household;
5. the persons who regularly operate a covered auto ;
6. an operator's marital status; or
- 7 . the driver's license or operator's permit status of you , a relative , or a rated resident.

## SETTLEMENT OF CLAIMS

We may use estimating, appraisal, or injury evaluation systems to assist us in adjusting claims under this policy and to assist us in determining the amount of damages, expenses, or loss payable under this policy . Such systems may be developed by us or a third party and may include computer software, databases, and specialized technology.

## TERMS OF POLICY CONFORMED TO STATUTES

If any provision of this policy fails to conform to the statutes of the state listed on your application as your residence, the provision shall be deemed amended to conform to such statutes. All other provisions shall be given full force and effect. Any disputes as to the coverages provided or the provisions of this policy shall be governed by the law of the state listed on your application as your residence.

## TRANSFER OF INTEREST

The rights and duties under this policy may not be transferred to another person without our written consent. However, if a named insured shown on the declarations page dies, this policy will provide coverage until the end of the policy period for the legal representative of the named insured, while acting as such, and for persons covered under this policy on the date of the named insured's death.

## FRAUD OR MISREPRESENTATION

Any changes we make at your request to this policy after inception will be made in reliance upon information you provide. If you :

- 1 . make incorrect statements or representations to us with regard to any material fact or circumstance;
2. conceal or misrepresent any material fact or circumstance; or
3. engage in fraudulent conduct;

we may deny coverage for an accident or loss if you , in connection with any requested change, or at any time during the policy period, have concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance or engaged in fraudulent conduct and that concealment, misrepresentation, or fraudulent conduct was material to a risk we assumed.

We may deny coverage for an accident or loss if you or a person seeking coverage has concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, or engaged in fraudulent conduct which materially affects our interests, in connection with the presentation or settlement of a claim.

## PAYMENT OF PREMIUM AND FEES

In addition to premium, fees may be charged on your policy . We may charge fees for installment payments, late payments, and other transactions. Fees may also be charged if you tender a check, draft, electronic funds transfer, or other type of remittance to us for any full or partial payment of your premium, and the method of such payment is returned to us or refused because of insufficient funds, a closed account, or a stop payment order. Payments made on your policy will be applied first to fees, then to premium due.

## CANCELLATION

You may cancel this policy during the policy period by calling or writing us and stating the future date you wish the cancellation to be effective.

We may cancel this policy during the policy period by mailing a notice of cancellation to the named insured shown on the declarations page at the last known address appearing in our records.

If the policy is cancelled for nonpayment of premium, we will mail notice of cancellation to you at least 15 days before cancellation takes effect. In all other cases, we will mail notice of cancellation to you at least 25 days before the cancellation takes effect.

We may cancel this policy for any reason if the notice is received by the named insured within the first 59 days of the initial policy period.

After this policy is in effect for more than 59 days, or if this is a renewal or continuation policy , we may cancel only for one or more of the following reasons:

- 1 . nonpayment of premium;
2. material misrepresentation or fraud by you with respect to any material fact in the procurement, continuation, change or renewal of this policy;
3. material misrepresentation or fraud in the submission of any claim under this policy;
4. loss of driving privileges through suspension, revocation or expiration of an operator's license issued to you , any driver in your household, or any regular operator of a covered auto , other than the first or second suspension under:
- a. Title 29-A M.R.S.A §2471(2);
- b. Title 29-A M.R.S.A §2472(2); or
- c. Title 28-A M.R.S.A §2052;
5. loss of driving privileges by you , a relative , a rated resident , or a principal operator of a covered auto through revocation of an operator's license during the policy period or if this policy is a renewal, during its policy period or the 180 days immediately preceding its effective date; or
6. violation of the terms or conditions of this policy .

A postal service certificate of mailing to the named insured at the insured's last known address appearing in our records will be sufficient proof of notice. If this policy is cancelled, coverage will not be provided as of the effective date and time shown in the notice of cancellation. For purposes of cancellation, this policy is neither severable nor divisible.  Any cancellation will be effective for all coverages for all persons and all vehicles.

## CANCELLATION REFUND

Upon cancellation, you may be entitled to a premium refund. However, our making or offering of a refund is not a condition of cancellation.

If this policy is cancelled, any refund due will be computed on a daily pro rata basis. However, we will retain a cancellation fee if this policy is cancelled at your request or if cancellation is for nonpayment of premium. A cancellation fee will be charged only during the initial policy period.

## NONRENEWAL

If neither we nor one of our affiliates offers to renew or continue this policy , we will mail notice of nonrenewal to the named insured shown on the declarations page at the last known address appearing in our records. A postal service certificate of mailing to the named insured at the insured's last known address appearing in our records will be sufficient proof of notice. Notice will be mailed more than 33 days before the end of the policy period.

## AUTOMATIC TERMINATION

If we or an affiliate offers to renew or continue this policy and you or your representative does not accept, this policy will automatically terminate at the end of the current policy period. Failure to pay the required renewal or continuation premium when due will mean that you have not accepted our offer.

If you obtain other insurance on a covered auto , any similar insurance provided by this policy will terminate as to that covered auto on the effective date of the other insurance.

If a covered auto is sold or transferred to someone other than you or a relative , any insurance provided by this policy will terminate as to that covered auto on the effective date of the sale or transfer.

## LIMITS OF LIABILITY

The limit of liability shown on the declarations page for  Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage is the most we will pay regardless of the number of:

2. covered autos ;
3. insured persons ;
4. lawsuits brought;
5. vehicles involved in the accident; or

## If your declarations page shows a split limit:

- 1 . the amount shown for 'each person' is the most we will pay for all damages due to bodily injury to one person; and
2. subject to the 'each person' limit, the amount shown for 'each accident' is the most we will pay for all damages due to bodily injury sustained by two or more persons in any one accident.

The 'each person' limit of liability includes the total of all claims made for bodily injury to an insured person and all claims of others derived from such bodily injury , including, but not limited to, emotional injury or mental anguish resulting from the bodily injury of another or from witnessing the bodily injury to another, loss of society , loss of companionship, loss of services, loss of consortium, and wrongful death.

If  the declarations  page shows  that  'combined  single  limit'  or  'CSL '  applies,  the amount shown is the most we will pay for the total of all damages resulting from any one accident. ## UNREASONABLE OR UNNECESSARY MEDICAL EXPENSES

If an insured person incurs expenses for medical services that we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary, we may refuse to pay for those expenses and contest them.

If the medical service provider sues the insured person because we refuse to pay expenses for medical services that we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary, we will pay any resulting defense costs, and any resulting judgment against the insured person , subject to the limit of liability for this coverage. We will choose the counsel. We will also pay reasonable expenses, including loss of earnings up to $200 per day, incurred at our request.

The insured person may not sue us for expenses for medical services we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary unless the insured person paid the entire disputed amount to the medical service provider or the medical service provider has initiated collection activity against the insured person for the unreasonable or unnecessary expenses.

## CHANGES

This policy contract, your insurance application (which is made a part of this policy as if attached hereto), the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy issued by us , contain all the agreements between you and us .   Subject to the following, the terms of this policy may not be changed or waived except by an endorsement issued by us .

If this information is determined by us to be incorrect, incomplete, or if it changes during the policy period, you agree that we may adjust your policy information and premium accordingly. Changes that may result in a premium adjustment are contained in our rates and rules. These include, but are not limited to, you , a relative , or a rated resident obtaining a driver's license or operator's permit, or changes in:

- 1 . the number, type or use classification of covered autos ;

## SETTLEMENT OF CLAIMS

## TERMS OF POLICY CONFORMED TO STATUTES

All other provisions shall be given full force and effect. Any disputes as to the coverages provided or the provisions of this policy shall be governed by the law of the state listed on your application as your residence.

## TRANSFER OF INTEREST

The rights and duties under this policy may not be transferred to another person without our written consent. we may deny coverage for an accident or loss if you , in connection with any requested change, or at any time during the policy period, have concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance or engaged in fraudulent conduct and that concealment, misrepresentation, or fraudulent conduct was material to a risk we assumed.

limits. However, any insurance we provide for a non-owned auto , or trailer not shown on the declarations page , will be excess over any other collectible source of recovery including, but not limited to:

- 1 . any coverage provided by the owner of the non-owned auto or trailer ;

## APPRAISAL

If we cannot agree with you on the amount of a loss, then we or you may demand an appraisal of the loss. Within 30 days of any demand for an appraisal, each party shall appoint a competent appraiser and shall notify the other party of that appraiser's identity . The appraisers will determine the amount of loss. If they fail to agree, the disagreement will be submitted to a qualified umpire chosen by the appraisers. If the two appraisers are unable to agree upon an umpire within 15 days, we or you may request that a judge of a court of record, in the county where you reside, select an umpire. The appraisers and umpire will determine the amount of loss. The amount of loss agreed to by both appraisers, or by one appraiser and the umpire, will be binding. You will pay your appraiser's fees and expenses. We will pay our appraiser's fees and expenses. All other expenses of the appraisal, including payment of the umpire if one is selected, will be shared equally between us and you . ## TERMS OF POLICY CONFORMED TO STATUTES

If any provision of this policy fails to conform to the statutes of the state listed on your application as your residence, the provision shall be deemed amended to conform to such statutes. All other provisions shall be given full force and effect. ## TRANSFER OF INTEREST

The rights and duties under this policy may not be transferred to another person without our written consent. Any changes we make at your request to this policy after inception will be made in reliance upon information you provide. If you :

- 1 . make incorrect statements or representations to us with regard to any material fact or circumstance;

we may deny coverage for an accident or loss if you , in connection with any requested change, or at any time during the policy period, have concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance or engaged in fraudulent conduct and that concealment, misrepresentation, or fraudulent conduct was material to a risk we assumed.

## CHANGES

This policy contract, your insurance application (which is made a part of this policy as if attached hereto), the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy issued by us , contain all the agreements between you and us .   Subject to the following, the terms of this policy may not be changed or waived except by an endorsement issued by us .

The premium for this policy is based on information we received from you and other sources. You agree to cooperate with us in determining if this information is correct and complete, and to promptly notify us if it changes during the policy period. If this information is determined by us to be incorrect, incomplete, or if it changes during the policy period, you agree that we may adjust your policy information and premium accordingly. Changes that may result in a premium adjustment are contained in our rates and rules. These include, but are not limited to, you , a relative , or a rated resident obtaining a driver's license or operator's permit, or changes in:

- 1 . the number, type or use classification of covered autos ;
2. the persons who regularly operate a covered auto ;
3. the persons of legal driving age residing in your household;
4. the residents in your household;
5. an operator's marital status;
6. your mailing address and your residence address;
- 7 . the principal garaging address of any covered auto ;
8. coverage, deductibles, or limits of liability; or
9. rating territory or discount eligibility .

The coverage provided in your policy may be changed only by the issuance of a new policy or an endorsement by us .  However, if during the policy period we broaden any coverage afforded under the current edition of your policy without additional premium charge, that change will automatically apply to your policy as of the date the coverage change is implemented in your state.

If you ask us to delete a vehicle from this policy , no coverage will apply to that vehicle as of the date and time you ask us to delete it.

## DUTY TO REPORT CHANGES

You must promptly report to us all changes, including additions and deletions, in policy information. This includes, but is not limited to, changes in:

- 1 . your mailing address or your residence address;
2. the principal garaging address of any covered auto ;
3. the residents in your household;
4. the persons of legal driving age residing in your household;
5. the persons who regularly operate a covered auto ;
6. an operator's marital status; or
- 7 . the driver's license or operator's permit status of you , a relative , or a rated resident.

## SETTLEMENT OF CLAIMS

We may use estimating, appraisal, or injury evaluation systems to assist us in adjusting claims under this policy and to assist us in determining the amount of damages, expenses, or loss payable under this policy . Such systems may be developed by us or a third party and may include computer software, databases, and specialized technology.

## TERMS OF POLICY CONFORMED TO STATUTES

If any provision of this policy fails to conform to the statutes of the state listed on your application as your residence, the provision shall be deemed amended to conform to such statutes. All other provisions shall be given full force and effect. Any disputes as to the coverages provided or the provisions of this policy shall be governed by the law of the state listed on your application as your residence.

## TRANSFER OF INTEREST

The rights and duties under this policy may not be transferred to another person without our written consent. However, if a named insured shown on the declarations page dies, this policy will provide coverage until the end of the policy period for the legal representative of the named insured, while acting as such, and for persons covered under this policy on the date of the named insured's death.

## FRAUD OR MISREPRESENTATION

Any changes we make at your request to this policy after inception will be made in reliance upon information you provide. If you :

- 1 . make incorrect statements or representations to us with regard to any material fact or circumstance;

3. engage in fraudulent conduct;

we may deny coverage for an accident or loss if you , in connection with any requested change, or at any time during the policy period, have concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance or engaged in fraudulent conduct and that concealment, misrepresentation, or fraudulent conduct was material to a risk we assumed.

We may deny coverage for an accident or loss if you or a person seeking coverage has concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, or engaged in fraudulent conduct which materially affects our interests, in connection with the presentation or settlement of a claim.

## PAYMENT OF PREMIUM AND FEES

In addition to premium, fees may be charged on your policy . We may charge fees for installment payments, late payments, and other transactions. Fees may also be charged if you tender a check, draft, electronic funds transfer, or other type of remittance to us for any full or partial payment of your premium, and the method of such payment is returned to us or refused because of insufficient funds, a closed account, or a stop payment order. If you or the person seeking coverage cannot identify the owner or operator of a vehicle involved in the accident, or if theft or vandalism has occurred, you or the person seeking coverage must notify the police within 24 hours or as soon as practicable.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COLLISION COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , resulting from collision .

In addition, we will pay the reasonable cost to replace any child safety seat damaged in an accident to which this coverage applies.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COMPREHENSIVE COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , that is not caused by collision .

## A loss not caused by collision includes:

- 1 . contact with an animal (including a bird);
2. explosion or earthquake;
3. fire;
4. malicious mischief or vandalism;
5. missiles or falling objects;
6. riot or civil commotion;
- 7 . theft or larceny;
8. windstorm, hail, water or flood; or
9. breakage of glass not caused by collision .

## In addition, we will pay for:

- 1 . reasonable transportation expenses incurred by you if a covered auto is stolen; and
2. loss of use damages that you are legally liable to pay if a non-owned auto is stolen. A combined maximum of $900, not exceeding $30 per day, will apply to these additional benefits. 2. when the auto has been recovered and repaired;

4. 72 hours after we make an offer to settle the loss if the auto is deemed by us to be a total loss; or

5. if the loss is theft of a rented non-owned auto , 30 days after loss of use begins on the loss.

We must receive written proof of transportation expenses and loss of use damages.

## CHANGES

This policy contract, your insurance application (which is made a part of this policy as if attached hereto), the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy issued by us , contain all the agreements between you and us .   Subject to the following, the terms of this policy may not be changed or waived except by an endorsement issued by us .

The premium for this policy is based on information we received from you and other sources. You agree to cooperate with us in determining if this information is correct and complete, and to promptly notify us if it changes during the policy period. If this information is determined by us to be incorrect, incomplete, or if it changes during the policy period, you agree that we may adjust your policy information and premium accordingly. Changes that may result in a premium adjustment are contained in our rates and rules. These include, but are not limited to, you , a relative , or a rated resident obtaining a driver's license or operator's permit, or changes in:

- 1 . the number, type or use classification of covered autos ;

5. an operator's marital status;
6. your mailing address and your residence address;
- 7 . the principal garaging address of any covered auto ;
8. coverage, deductibles, or limits of liability; or
9. rating territory or discount eligibility .

The coverage provided in your policy may be changed only by the issuance of a new policy or an endorsement by us .  However, if during the policy period we broaden any coverage afforded under the current edition of your policy without additional premium charge, that change will automatically apply to your policy as of the date the coverage change is implemented in your state.

## DUTY TO REPORT CHANGES

You must promptly report to us all changes, including additions and deletions, in policy information. This includes, but is not limited to, changes in:

- 1 . your mailing address or your residence address;

## SETTLEMENT OF CLAIMS

We may use estimating, appraisal, or injury evaluation systems to assist us in adjusting claims under this policy and to assist us in determining the amount of damages, expenses, or loss payable under this policy . Such systems may be developed by us or a third party and may include computer software, databases, and specialized technology.

## TERMS OF POLICY CONFORMED TO STATUTES

If any provision of this policy fails to conform to the statutes of the state listed on your application as your residence, the provision shall be deemed amended to conform to such statutes. All other provisions shall be given full force and effect. Any disputes as to the coverages provided or the provisions of this policy shall be governed by the law of the state listed on your application as your residence.

## TRANSFER OF INTEREST

The rights and duties under this policy may not be transferred to another person without our written consent. However, if a named insured shown on the declarations page dies, this policy will provide coverage until the end of the policy period for the legal representative of the named insured, while acting as such, and for persons covered under this policy on the date of the named insured's death.

## FRAUD OR MISREPRESENTATION

Any changes we make at your request to this policy after inception will be made in reliance upon information you provide. If you :

- 1 . make incorrect statements or representations to us with regard to any material fact or circumstance;
2. conceal or misrepresent any material fact or circumstance; or
3. engage in fraudulent conduct;

we may deny coverage for an accident or loss if you , in connection with any requested change, or at any time during the policy period, have concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance or engaged in fraudulent conduct and that concealment, misrepresentation, or fraudulent conduct was material to a risk we assumed.

We may deny coverage for an accident or loss if you or a person seeking coverage has concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, or engaged in fraudulent conduct which materially affects our interests, in connection with the presentation or settlement of a claim.

## PAYMENT OF PREMIUM AND FEES

In addition to premium, fees may be charged on your policy . We may charge fees for installment payments, late payments, and other transactions. Fees may also be charged if you tender a check, draft, electronic funds transfer, or other type of remittance to us for any full or partial payment of your premium, and the method of such payment is returned to us or refused because of insufficient funds, a closed account, or a stop payment order. ## CHANGES

This policy contract, your insurance application (which is made a part of this policy as if attached hereto), the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy issued by us , contain all the agreements between you and us .   Subject to the following, the terms of this policy may not be changed or waived except by an endorsement issued by us .

If this information is determined by us to be incorrect, incomplete, or if it changes during the policy period, you agree that we may adjust your policy information and premium accordingly. Changes that may result in a premium adjustment are contained in our rates and rules. These include, but are not limited to, you , a relative , or a rated resident obtaining a driver's license or operator's permit, or changes in:

- 1 . the number, type or use classification of covered autos ;

5. an operator's marital status;

8. coverage, deductibles, or limits of liability; or
9. rating territory or discount eligibility .

The coverage provided in your policy may be changed only by the issuance of a new policy or an endorsement by us .  However, if during the policy period we broaden any coverage afforded under the current edition of your policy without additional premium charge, that change will automatically apply to your policy as of the date the coverage change is implemented in your state.

If you ask us to delete a vehicle from this policy , no coverage will apply to that vehicle as of the date and time you ask us to delete it.

## DUTY TO REPORT CHANGES

You must promptly report to us all changes, including additions and deletions, in policy information. This includes, but is not limited to, changes in:

- 1 . your mailing address or your residence address;

We may use estimating, appraisal, or injury evaluation systems to assist us in adjusting claims under this policy and to assist us in determining the amount of damages, expenses, or loss payable under this policy . Such systems may be developed by us or a third party and may include computer software, databases, and specialized technology.

## TERMS OF POLICY CONFORMED TO STATUTES

If any provision of this policy fails to conform to the statutes of the state listed on your application as your residence, the provision shall be deemed amended to conform to such statutes. All other provisions shall be given full force and effect. Any disputes as to the coverages provided or the provisions of this policy shall be governed by the law of the state listed on your application as your residence.

## TRANSFER OF INTEREST

The rights and duties under this policy may not be transferred to another person without our written consent. However, if a named insured shown on the declarations page dies, this policy will provide coverage until the end of the policy period for the legal representative of the named insured, while acting as such, and for persons covered under this policy on the date of the named insured's death.

## FRAUD OR MISREPRESENTATION

Any changes we make at your request to this policy after inception will be made in reliance upon information you provide. If you :

- 1 . make incorrect statements or representations to us with regard to any material fact or circumstance;
2. conceal or misrepresent any material fact or circumstance; or
3. engage in fraudulent conduct;

we may deny coverage for an accident or loss if you , in connection with any requested change, or at any time during the policy period, have concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance or engaged in fraudulent conduct and that concealment, misrepresentation, or fraudulent conduct was material to a risk we assumed.

We may deny coverage for an accident or loss if you or a person seeking coverage has concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, or engaged in fraudulent conduct which materially affects our interests, in connection with the presentation or settlement of a claim.

## PAYMENT OF PREMIUM AND FEES

In addition to premium, fees may be charged on your policy . We may charge fees for installment payments, late payments, and other transactions. Fees may also be charged if you tender a check, draft, electronic funds transfer, or other type of remittance to us for any full or partial payment of your premium, and the method of such payment is returned to us or refused because of insufficient funds, a closed account, or a stop payment order.
